title: Gothic crossing of the Danube
summary: In 376 CE, Gothic Tervingi and Greuthungi displaced by the Huns sought asylum in the Eastern Roman Empire and crossed the lower Danube into Thrace. Exploitation and mistreatment by Roman commanders provoked a major Gothic uprising that culminated in the catastrophic Roman defeat at Adrianople.

uncertainty.note: Summer to autumn 376 CE; Ammianus Marcellinus does not record exact calendar days for the crossing.

as_recorded.value: In the year 376, the Goths sent a request to cross the Danube into Roman territory.

where.modern_name: Silistra, Bulgaria (Durostorum on the lower Danube)

importance.justification: Admitting the armed Gothic nation across the Danube permanently altered Roman frontier security and triggered the Gothic War that destroyed an imperial field army at Adrianople.

related.because: Roman mistreatment of the Goths after the crossing led directly to the Gothic rebellion and battle of Adrianople.

beats.caption: In 376, thousands of Gothic refugees cross the lower Danube into Roman Thrace with imperial permission.
